title: PowerToys Run: one-off startup crash – PowerToys.ManagedCommon 0.98.1.0 not found
author: boardtc

judgment.rationale: The one-off assembly-load failure occurred on an old mixed 0.98.0/0.98.1 installation, PowerToys subsequently worked normally, and the reporter has now said they have supplied everything they know and are comfortable with closure. There is no reproducible current defect to investigate.
evidence: The exception requests PowerToys.ManagedCommon 0.98.1.0 while the crash report identifies PowerToys 0.98.0.0.
The reporter says the error occurred once and PowerToys continued to work normally afterward.
No reliable reproduction steps or diagnostic archive are available.
The automated upstream triage comment requested current-version confirmation and reproduction details.
The reporter replied that they have added everything they know and suggested closing the issue if the report is not useful.
judgment.recommended_action: Close the issue as not currently actionable, while inviting a new report with current-version diagnostics if the assembly mismatch recurs.

fix_assessment.rationale: The available evidence points to a transient mixed-version installation from an obsolete release. A current repository fix cannot be selected until recurrence on a supported version or installation diagnostics identify an active servicing defect.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run failed once because a 0.98.0 process requested a 0.98.1 ManagedCommon assembly, then resumed working normally. The reporter cannot provide additional evidence and is open to closure.
known_information: The exception is a FileNotFoundException for PowerToys.ManagedCommon version 0.98.1.0.
The crash metadata reports PowerToys version 0.98.0.0.
PowerToys was installed through auto-update and had worked on the machine for about a year.
The event is not reliably reproducible and no bug-report ZIP is attached.
An upstream automated triage comment requested reproduction details and an update to the latest stable release.
The reporter replied that they have provided all available information and suggested closure if it is insufficient.
inferences: A partial or interrupted historical update may have temporarily mixed binaries from 0.98.0 and 0.98.1, but this is not confirmed.
Because the application subsequently worked, the mismatched state may already have self-repaired or been transient.
issue_context.analysis: The assembly versions provide a historical servicing signal but not a current actionable code path. The author response resolves the waiting state without adding evidence that supports investigation. A concise closure recommendation is appropriate, while a future reproducible current-version occurrence should be filed with fresh diagnostics.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, labels, and existing automated triage response.
Confirmed that the only concrete failure evidence is a mixed 0.98.0/0.98.1 assembly version and that the issue supplies no repeatable trigger.
No linked current fix attempt or duplicate is present in the issue timeline.
Read the reporter's latest response and confirmed that no additional reproduction or diagnostic evidence is available.

information_gaps.information: Whether the failure reproduces after updating to the current stable PowerToys release.
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether an active servicing or binding defect remains.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Update to the latest stable release and report whether PowerToys Run fails again.

information_gaps.information: A fresh diagnostic archive captured immediately after any recurrence.
information_gaps.why_needed: Installer and runtime logs are needed to distinguish an interrupted update from another assembly-resolution failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: If the problem recurs, immediately submit a comment containing /bugreport.

comment.body: Thanks for sharing all the information you have. Since this was a one-off failure on the older 0.98.x installation, PowerToys continued working afterward, and there is no current reproduction or diagnostic report to investigate, we can close this for now. If the same assembly-loading error occurs again on the latest stable PowerToys release, please open a new issue and submit `/bugreport` immediately after the failure so we can inspect the update and runtime logs.
